_comment: Non-role address-kind registry (Ruling 13, de5d538f, thread f60b8eb4). Complements config/roles/roles.json: every registered to:-address is either a key under roles.json.roles (kind=role — the only kind carrying a delivery obligation) or a key under addresses here. kind=alias: accepted at write, never rejected; expansion-at-write is R13 Phase C, and the expansion-target decisions are now MADE - each alias carries an `expansion.mode` plus ruling and rationale (Ruling 26 §§1-5; targets for leader/designer/watchdog in §§5, ratified Ruling 27). Aliases deliberately carry NO `targets` key: the target set is derived, and an explicit list would be a second, silently-ignored source of truth. kind=telemetry: recorded for the historical record, never delivered, no inbox pointer, never a role. Non-role addresses must NOT be added to roles.json.roles. INVARIANT (Ruling 24, 8a466f98) - the roles<->delivery relation is a UNION, NOT equality: roles.json (union) address-kinds.json is a SUBSET OF tackle.roles, and tackle.roles is permitted to be a STRICT SUPERSET. The two tables do different jobs: tackle.roles is the DELIVERY vocabulary, while this pair is the REGISTRY. A registered non-role address may legitimately hold a delivery row - that row records the address, not a delivery obligation - and `delivery: never` constrains the inbox pointer, not row existence. So neither side implies the other: a key here need NOT appear in tackle.roles, and a tackle.roles name need NOT appear here. Equality would compel the withdrawn `DELETE FROM tackle.roles WHERE name='big-pickle'` (tester e5538da4, upheld-as-retracted and moot in Ruling 24 section 4).

wr-conf-observer.description: Work-request-conf observer stream — ARCHIVAL telemetry. Recorded, never delivered; no inbox pointer; no harness/persona surfaces; do NOT register as a role; do NOT retag historical entries (retagging would flood a NULL-pointer mailbox).
wr-conf-observer.completionMarker: stream closed at the 2026-09-21 session-protocol boundary; all entries are immutable archival history — no delivery expected in any window

expansion.rationale: Expand-and-replace over every roles.json kind:role key. Single-hop: expansion sources are kind:role entries only, never aliases, so fan-out is flat (|roles| = 28 today) and alias cycles are inexpressible. Snapshot-at-write: the set freezes when the record is written, so registering role #29 does not retroactively deliver historical to:all records. Dedupe against explicit tags. NO `targets` key by design — the target set is derived, and an explicit list would be a second, silently-ignored source of truth.

Implied by §3.1 alongside `all`. Being a superset of `all` is harmless precisely because single-hop forbids alias->alias expansion; if alias-to-alias were ever permitted this address would expand to `all` + 28 roles and become an exponential blow-up with a cycle risk.

One record, ONE Assembly thread. Expand-and-replace is actively harmful here — fanning out would create N duplicate threads in a shared surface, corrupting thread ordering and directly damaging R8.1 PR-scan title matching. Not telemetry either: it produces a delivered, human-read artifact. Three binding negatives: no per-role fan-out (the forum write IS the delivery), NO inbox-pointer advance for any role (else R17 pointers credit roles with unread messages), and never reject. The `to:assembly` tag is RETAINED on the record as provenance. NO `targets` key.

Resolves to the creating record's own role. Deterministic is not the same as always resolvable: if the writer has no role (a service, a harness, a direct-DB writer — this system has all three), `to:self` does NOT expand and emits WARN `unresolvable-self`. It must never fall back to `to:all` or `to:user`, which would redirect a self-addressed record to an unrelated audience. NO `targets` key — the target is the writer, known only at write time.

Single recipient — the operator identity — via the response-app notification path (service :4400 -> /response UI :4299). Closes the historical gap where exclusive `to:user` records (4 corpus) were never delivered; expansion fixes it going forward only (R13 write-side-only, historical records untouched). Two required constraints: NON-BLOCKING, and absence must be observable — if the operator is not present the notification queues or defers, it must not block the write and must not vanish silently. Single point accepted deliberately: fanning `to:user` across roles would deliver private operator-directed traffic to roles never addressed. No fan-out, no pointer movement, never reject. NO `targets` key.

expansion.rationale: A model identity carries no delivery obligation. delivery='never' below. NO `targets` key.

big-pickle.description: Model-name harness alias (opencode/big-pickle). Excluded from roles.json structurally: correct by construction, whereas an in-place kind=alias would be correct only if EVERY consumer honoured kind.

expansion.rationale: Declared UNMAPPED. Per Ruling 26 §5, `targets` absent or empty means: on write, no expansion, WARN `alias-unmapped`, NEVER reject. This is the declared-unmapped state, not the §0 silent-drop — the failure is visible and guarded. Ruling 26 §5 states Phase C is NOT blocked on this. The lookup is delivered (see dbaNote); what remains is an architect ruling.

admin.dbaNote: LOOKUP DELIVERED, NOT WRITTEN (DBA record 7964a091, Ruling 26 §5). Recommended targets: ["sysadmin"] — the only admin-semantics kind:role key in roles.json (28 keys @ 325a7e33d). BLOCKED on an architect ruling, not on further lookup: assembly.users carries a live row aliased `admin` (9abe1316-312e-4a2f-96ad-88c4b86c7b1e, admin=true, admin@nexus.com — the only such row of 36), but `admin` is not a roles.json key, so Ruling 26 §5 single-hop makes the Assembly-admin reading structurally unreachable. Options: (a) targets=["sysadmin"], reversible, does not move the Ruling 26 §1 fan-out bound; (b) mint `admin` as a 29th kind:role key, which moves that bound 28->29 and requires a tackle.roles row. Left unmapped so the guard fails loudly per Ruling 26 §5, never silently.
